timing.note: Wall clock per frame including the bridge round trip. 1600x900 was measured once on the same model at the same Medium quality. Every thumbnail carries a 0.25 min (15 s) progressive_maxTime budget that Benton's own settings do not have -- his leave it at 0.0, meaning no limit.

1.what: environment and sun, exterior camera, driven through WR_SunAim.light_it_from_here

fixed.lights: as found (and therefore absent - see findings.hidden_light_tag)

1.carry_basis: image-qa mean luminance closest to 0.40 among PASSing arms - a mechanical tie-break, NOT a look verdict

2.what: room-versus-booth light balance, BOTH cameras, WR Lights tag forced visible

3.what: five-step EV ladder on both cameras against three rigs

8.what: one 800x450 interior frame for the foam question

9.what: probe frames that proved the light rig was absent from the render

hidden_light_tag.statement: The SketchUp tag "WR Lights" was HIDDEN, so none of the eight rectangle lights were exported and NO render in this model has ever contained artificial light.
hidden_light_tag.evidence: With the sun disabled and the interior camera at EV 9, lights-on, lights-off and booth-at-20x all measured mean luminance 0.05130 - identical to five decimal places. Tag visibility read false directly off model.layers.
hidden_light_tag.consequence: Pass 2's "8x room-to-booth imbalance" was never in the pictures. The reason one EV could not serve both views is that the booth interior had no light source at all, only sky spill.

true_ratio.statement: With the tag shown, the as-found rig is room:booth = 22.72 : 1 by summed intensity, not the ~8x assumed in pass 2.

single_ev.statement: As found, NO single EV serves both views. With the booth fixture raised, one EV does.

evidence.asfound: every EV either blows the exterior (8.0-11.0) or crushes the interior (12.5-14.0); no row passes both
evidence.booth16x: EV 12.5 AND EV 14.0 both pass both - a two-stop window
evidence.note: EV 14.0 is within 0.23 of Benton's own untouched camera (f/8 @ 1/300, ISO 100 = EV 14.23), so at booth16x his configured camera serves both views with nothing written to /CameraPhysical.

standard_light.statement: /Standard Light (intensity 2500, the largest number in the rig) contributes nothing - the stdoff arm is identical to asfound to three decimals.

foam.statement: The blue acoustic foam wedge geometry SURVIVES into the render intact; the material does not.
foam.geometry: definition "Foam", 1447 faces, 2 instances, tag WR-Booth-Foam visible. The 800x450 interior frame shows the pyramidal wedge field with clear relief and self-shadowing.
foam.material: All 1447 faces carry "Color_I06", which in the V-Ray scene is a _HostMaterial pass-through with NO /VRay Mtl child, no reflection layer, no roughness and no texture - pure flat diffuse. By contrast "Bass Trap Gray" is a real MtlSingleBRDF with a /VRay Mtl and a TexBitmap, and reads as a material.
foam.note: Reported, not fixed - library materials live on P: which is read only.

hdri.statement: ATTEMPTED AND FAILED. V-Ray does ship HDRIs locally, so the arm was not skipped for lack of a file.
files_found: C:/Program Files/Chaos/V-Ray/V-Ray for SketchUp/extension/integration/resources/Default Dome Light Texture.exr
hdri.why_failed: A TexBitmap + BitmapBuffer pair can be created and deleted cleanly via VRay::Scene#create/#delete, and the buffer accepts the file path. But assigning that texture into /SettingsEnvironment bg_tex/gi_tex/reflect_tex/refract_tex does not stick - the slots read back /Environment Sky. The two frames this produced were therefore duplicates of the sun-off arm and were DELETED rather than shipped as an HDRI arm.
hdri.next_step: VRay::Command.create_dome_light exists on this build and is the more likely route; failing that, set the dome in the Asset Editor by hand and re-run the sweep.

safe_frame.statement: Safe Frame could NOT be turned on from Ruby. It is /SettingsOutput userdata show_safe_frames, currently 0.
safe_frame.why: Writing show_safe_frames inside a VRay::Scene#change never returns - Ruby wedges with no dialog on screen and the SketchUp process has to be killed. This happened twice and cost two restarts.
safe_frame.action: Benton must tick it in the V-Ray UI. The harness now refuses the write by name.
